svg.title: Summing a 3-by-3 array along each axis
svg.desc: Three hand-drawn panels reducing the same three-by-three array of one through nine. The first, np.sum of a with no axis, outlines the whole grid and produces the scalar forty-five. The second, axis equals nought, outlines each column and collapses the rows, producing twelve, fifteen, eighteen of shape three. The third, axis equals one, outlines each row and collapses the columns, producing six, fifteen, twenty-four, also of shape three. In every panel the slices being collapsed are outlined on the source grid itself. A band states that the axis named in the call is the axis that disappears, and notes that both reductions return a one-dimensional shape of three, which is where the silent broadcasting bug begins.
svg.text: The same nine numbers, reduced three ways. The axis named in the call is the axis that disappears.
The axis you name is the axis that disappears.
Both reductions return shape (3,) here, and that 1-D shape is where the next figure’s bug begins.
